instruction.name: setx86j
instruction.description: ARM-style set-if-condition: evaluate condition code `cond` against the flag register and write 1 or 0 to `rd`.

latencies.notes: EFLAGS -> rd: the condition is evaluated against the flag register and the chain closes through `x86mtflag`, so the measured 3.00 cycles less the 2-cycle flag move give 1.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4
throughput.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 2000 --unroll2 8000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'li.d $r12, 5; li.d $r13, 7; x86mtflag $r12, 0x3f; armmtflag $r12, 0xff' --asm 'setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4; setx86j $r12, 4'
throughput.notes: Reads the flag register and writes a GPR, so the copies do not chain and 1 CPI is a real throughput.

notes: LBT conditional set, measured with the flag register primed from a GPR in `--init`.
